title: VESIM Mumbai Hosts AHEAD 2026 International Conference on Inclusive Digital Education
summary: VES Institute of Management Studies and Research, Mumbai, hosted AHEAD 2026, a three-day hybrid conference under the EU's Erasmus+ AIDEdu project with delegates from India, Europe and Nepal.
body_html:
Mumbai, 12 November 2026: Vivekanand Education Society’s Institute of Management Studies and Research (VESIM), Mumbai, has hosted AHEAD 2026, the International Conference on Accessible, Holistic and Equitable Advancement through Digital Education. The three-day hybrid conference was organised under AIDEdu, a Capacity Building in Higher Education project co-funded by the European Union’s Erasmus+ programme, and brought together academicians, researchers, institutional leaders and international delegates from Europe, India and Nepal.

Prof. Dr. Badri Narayan Tiwari, Vice Chancellor, Tata Institute of Social Sciences (TISS), Mumbai, attended the inaugural ceremony as Guest of Honour. Dr. Doris Kiendl, Institute Chair, FH JOANNEUM, Austria, and Dr. Bal Krishna Bal, Dean, Kathmandu University, Nepal, were the Chief Guests.

The conference featured 79 scheduled research paper presentation slots across 12 groups, on topics including AI in education, digital learning, inclusive pedagogies and educational sustainability. Presentations were made in person, online and by video, with 24 reviewers and 20 session chairs supporting the sessions. Dr. Rupert Beinhauer of FH JOANNEUM, Austria, moderated an international panel discussion on ‘Accessible, Inclusive and Digital Education in Higher Education Institutions for Sustainable Development Goals’.

Ahead of the conference, the Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Teaching and Learning at VESIM conducted a two-day online faculty workshop, which received 121 registrations from 17 institutes, including eight foreign universities and 10 Indian universities.

Speaking about the conference, Dr. Vijay T. Raisinghani, Director, VESIM, said, “AHEAD 2026 provided an important platform for academicians and researchers from different countries to exchange ideas and share perspectives on the future of higher education. As digital technologies continue to shape teaching and learning, it is important for institutions to ensure that these advancements are accessible and inclusive. Through initiatives such as AIDEdu, VESIM remains committed to strengthening academic collaboration and supporting the development of more equitable and digitally enabled learning environments.”

Dr. Shalini Bariar, Professor and Head – International Relations, VESIM, said, “Leading the AIDEdu project has been a significant opportunity to strengthen international academic collaboration and advance the cause of accessible and inclusive digital higher education, while contributing to SDGs 4, 10 and 17. The initiative reflects our collective commitment to leveraging digital innovation to make higher education more equitable, inclusive and accessible, while building stronger global partnerships for the future.”

AIDEdu aims to strengthen institutional capacity and promote accessible, inclusive and digitally enabled management education. Selected research contributions from the conference are being compiled into an edited volume titled Education for an Equitable Future: Best Practices in Digital and Inclusive Higher Education for SDGs, with 26 chapters by authors from seven countries.
